decision: Recommend Option C (status quo + targeted hardening) at HIGH conviction, rejecting both consolidation directions
rationale: Trading-state safety is structurally preserved by dual-store (Wave 4 incidents only degraded dashboard, never trade state); bidirectional command queue blocks vanilla Litestream; tests are 100% SQLite-fixture-bound; Wave 4 already closed the Critical-severity sync bugs; remaining pain is mostly latent or continuous-low-grade and amenable to harden tasks
alternatives_considered: Option A (all-Postgres) — rejected: safety regression on trading + 1-3 person-weeks migration cost
Option B1/Litestream — rejected: incompatible with bidirectional pull_commands
Option B2/Turso — rejected: vendor risk on trading hot path
Option B3/Cloudflare Tunnel — deferred pending operator dashboard-usage data

decision: Absorb Option D (DB-engine abstraction at src/utils/db.py) into Option C as harden task H1
rationale: The abstraction is the single highest-leverage harden task regardless of consolidation choice; keeping it as a standalone option creates a false trichotomy with A/B/C; the actionable form IS H1, not a separate "do D, then decide" gate
alternatives_considered: Treat D as a separate "first do this, then decide between A/B/C in 3-6 months" path (rejected: same migration cost, same outcome)
Skip the abstraction entirely under Option C (rejected: loses the highest-leverage harden task)

decision: Flag Render PG monthly bill as ASSUMED, not computed
rationale: render.yaml:32 sets sync: false — the Postgres tier is provisioned manually in the Render dashboard and not visible in repo; cost is a brief-required dimension but cannot be computed without operator-side info
alternatives_considered: Skip cost dimension altogether (rejected: brief required it)
Fabricate a number from public Render pricing (rejected: dishonest — better to be explicit about ASSUMED)

decision: Size H1 (DB-engine abstraction) at 5-7 days, Medium complexity
rationale: 6 verified dual-mode files × ~10-30 LOC each + new abstraction module + tests for placeholder rewriting + tests for error mapping + module-by-module migration discipline; mechanical refactor but with non-trivial design surface (RealDictCursor vs sqlite3.Row, transaction semantics)
alternatives_considered: Size as Low (rejected: too optimistic given placeholder-rewriting subtleties + 6 distinct call sites)
Size as High (rejected: no architectural unknown, just careful mechanical work)

decision: Size H4 (testcontainers-postgres CI job) as Medium complexity
rationale: Most cost is test inventory + selection (~20 representative tests covering sync mode classifications / ON CONFLICT / savepoint / DDL drift / strip-id), not infrastructure; pytest-postgresql is known-good library; CI integration mechanics are routine
alternatives_considered: Size as Low (rejected: test selection is real judgment, not boilerplate)
Skip entirely (rejected: closes the substrate of every SQLite/PG impedance bug class)

decision: Set the CLAUDE.md-codified test floor of 3682 as a HARD invariant in any migration path
rationale: CLAUDE.md enforces this as a CI baseline; current count is 4574 (verified `pytest --collect-only` on 2026-05-05); the floor is operator-codified and should be treated as non-negotiable; any test-touching migration must replace 1-for-1
alternatives_considered: Allow temporary test-count regression with explicit rollback gate (rejected: floor is operator-codified, not negotiable; the rollback gate can wrap test-runtime instead)

decision: Preserve trading-state sync-independence as a SAFETY PROPERTY worth explicit defense
rationale: Wave 4 H1/H2/H3 only ever degraded the dashboard, never trade state; reconciler reads MAX(updated_at) on local SQLite (`reconcile_state.py:32-44`); this property is non-trivial, undocumented anywhere prior to this audit, and currently free
alternatives_considered: Treat trading-state coupling to PG as acceptable tradeoff for cleaner architecture (rejected: dollar-loss potential is unbounded; the safety property is currently free; PG outage scenarios would freeze trading)

decision: Recommend testcontainers-postgres on a SEPARATE CI job (not every PR)
rationale: Every-PR adds 5-15 min latency + flakiness from PG container startup; weekly catches drift before prod release; matches arcis CI conventions; the value is in catching drift, not in synchronously gating every PR
alternatives_considered: Run on every PR (rejected: latency + flakiness)
Skip entirely (rejected: closes the largest remaining bug substrate)

decision: Refuse to recommend libsql/Turso (Option B2) without explicit operator vendor-risk acknowledgment
rationale: Operator's stated preference for battle-tested deps (psycopg2, pandas, scipy); Turso founded 2022 — a single company, on the trading hot path; vendor lock-in / acquisition / pricing-change risk all real; should not be a default recommendation without operator buy-in
alternatives_considered: Recommend Option B2 because of free-tier cost and bidirectional support (rejected: vendor risk on trading hot path is structurally serious)
Drop B2 entirely (rejected: it's a real option that should be acknowledged + revisitable)

decision: Include Cloudflare Tunnel (B3) as residual uncertainty rather than as a full option in §4
rationale: B3 trades dashboard availability for simplicity; brief flags dashboard as heavily-used but operator usage frequency is unmeasured; cannot evaluate B3 without that data; B3 is a real path if usage is low and worth keeping visible
alternatives_considered: Treat B3 as a full Option (rejected: lacks operator usage data)
Exclude entirely (rejected: it's a real cost-dominated winner if usage is low)

decision: Set H6 (target_host on pending_commands) as MEDIUM-LOW priority within harden bundle
rationale: Latent risk that only materializes if operator commits to backup-machine plans; backward-compatible on its own (NULL = current behavior); cheap to land but not the highest-leverage task
alternatives_considered: Skip (rejected: closes a real footgun cheaply)
Make it H1 (rejected: not the highest-leverage task; the dual-mode-branch removal is)

decision: Refuse to estimate person-weeks for Option A as a primary recommendation timeline
rationale: Operator-time is the scarcest resource; Option A's 1-3 person-weeks is real cost against $0 marginal benefit at current evidence; offering a calendar-time number would frame Option A as more recommendable than it is
alternatives_considered: Provide a calendar-time "if started today" answer for Option A (rejected: wrong framing because A isn't recommended)
Skip the cost discussion entirely (rejected: brief required cost dimension; the discussion belongs in §4.1 where Option A is sketched)

decision: Re-anchor all registry.py citations at the `name="..."` declaration line, not at attribute lines (sync_to_postgres, sync_mode)
rationale: Phase 7 feasibility caught systematic 11-29 line drift between the original audit's citations and the current 2495-line registry; the original spec was measured against a registry version ~200 lines shorter; anchoring at attribute lines is fragile because attributes move within their TableDef block; the `name="..."` declaration is the most stable, grep-friendly anchor and is unambiguous within each TableDef; this re-anchoring discipline is being recorded as a design decision so future spec authors keep citation accuracy strict
alternatives_considered: Anchor at `_register(TableDef(` opening (rejected: less directly grep-friendly than `name="foo"`)
Leave original drifted citations and add a reviewer-note (rejected: spec credibility rides on citation accuracy per operator strict-rigor directive)
